title: Long PLTR — DoD AI Demand Surge + Aug 3 AH Earnings with 15% Options-Implied Move
entry: Long PLTR $124–$130 on the July 30 open or intraday. PLTR at $127.50 is positioned ahead of two simultaneous catalysts: (1) Aug 3 AH Q2 2026 earnings with options pricing ~15% implied move (vs ~8% historical average for PLTR — elevated uncertainty priced), and (2) the Iran-US military escalation, which directly accelerates DoD AI budget commitments to PLTR's AIP (Artificial Intelligence Platform) decision-intelligence and drone-defense use cases. The IRGC attack on US Jordan forces on July 26 represents a kinetic engagement that triggers rapid procurement cycles for AI-enabled battlefield situational awareness — PLTR's core DoD revenue driver. Enter at market or on any intraday weakness toward $124. Do not chase above $133 if PLTR opens above that level on the MSFT Azure beat enthusiasm.
stop_loss: $117 daily close — at $117, PLTR has broken below the $120 psychological support level established during the July 14–20 consolidation. A close below $117 implies either (1) a macro risk-off event (GDP hot print + AAPL AH miss + September hike probability above 75%) has overwhelmed the DoD catalyst thesis, selling PLTR alongside all growth equities regardless of the government contract thesis; or (2) a PLTR-specific negative event (loss of a major DoD contract renewal, congressional investigation of AIP contract award process, or key executive departure) has driven company-specific selling. The Iran-related DoD AI spending catalyst does not instantly translate to contract announcements — if the broader regime deteriorates sharply, PLTR can pull back to $117 even if the thesis remains structurally intact. Below $117, the position exits without waiting for the Aug 3 earnings catalyst.
targets: $140 — PLTR holds $125–$130 through July 30–Aug 2 on Iran/DoD macro backdrop; Aug 3 AH earnings confirm government revenue acceleration (US commercial + international government), US commercial revenue run rate above $600M annualized, Q3 FY26 guidance above consensus; options pricing validates with a 10%+ move on the print; +9.8% from $127.5 reference; cover 40% of position post-earnings open August 4

$155 — Post-earnings institutional accumulation: AIP is confirmed as the DoD AI middleware standard in the Aug 3 call (new contract disclosures, Pentagon AI program citations); sell-side upgrades follow with $170+ price targets; the Iran kinetic escalation becomes a sustained DoD budget argument (multi-year, not one-quarter); +21.6% from reference; cover 40% of remaining position

$170 — Full re-rating: PLTR recognized by DoD as the primary AI decision-intelligence platform for drone-defense and command-and-control; a major contract announcement ($2B+ TCV) in the Aug–Sep 2026 window; PLTR re-rates to 80x+ forward sales on the confirmed DoD monopoly thesis; hold final 20%
catalyst: Aug 3 AH Q2 2026 earnings: options pricing ~15% implied move vs ~8% historical average. Iran-US military exchange (IRGC attack on US Jordan forces July 26) is a direct DoD AI budget acceleration catalyst. AIP decision-intelligence and drone-defense use cases align directly with the escalated threat environment.
thesis:
Palantir occupies a unique position in today's market: it is simultaneously a DoD AI spending beneficiary, an AI infrastructure platform company with demonstrated commercial traction, and an earnings catalyst in four days. Most positions must choose one of these — PLTR has all three, which is why the options market is pricing a 15% implied move on Aug 3 AH (vs PLTR's 8% historical average earnings move). The elevated implied volatility does not represent overpricing; it represents genuine uncertainty about whether the DoD escalation narrative will arrive in the revenue line before the Street has a chance to model it.

The Iran-IRGC attack on US Jordan forces on July 26 is the specific catalyst that makes the DoD AI spending argument concrete rather than thematic. PLTR AIP has been deployed in the Pentagon's Maven Smart System (battlefield surveillance AI) and in drone-defense decision loops that require real-time threat classification at machine speed — exactly the use case that a IRGC attack on military personnel validates as a live operational requirement, not a future procurement scenario. Historical precedent: every kinetic engagement against US forces that triggers congressional attention to force protection technology has been followed within 90 days by an acceleration in DoD AI procurement. The July 26 Jordan attack is that trigger event for the Aug–Oct FY2026 budget supplemental cycle.

Commercially, PLTR's US commercial revenue has been the growth accelerator that re-rated the stock from a pure-government play to a diversified enterprise AI platform. The AIP bootcamp model — rapid prototype-to-production cycles that demonstrate ROI within weeks — has attracted Fortune 500 clients who cannot build internally what PLTR delivers commercially. If the Aug 3 call shows US commercial revenue on a $600M+ annualized run rate (from ~$500M in Q1), the DoD catalyst becomes additive to a thesis that is already working without the geopolitical premium. The two-pillar setup (government + commercial both accelerating simultaneously) is what produces the 15% implied move: the bear case is that government acceleration is a one-quarter DoD supplemental and commercial growth plateaus; the bull case is that both accelerate simultaneously and PLTR re-rates toward the $155–170 range by September.

The position horizon is intentionally short (1-2 weeks) to capture the earnings catalyst cleanly. After the Aug 3 print resolves the uncertainty, the position converts from an event trade to either a thesis hold (if both pillars confirm) or an exit (if the DoD acceleration doesn't appear in the revenue line). Size at 3% — the 15% implied move is symmetric; there is a 15% downside if the print disappoints and the Iran catalyst fails to translate to visible contract wins within this quarter's revenue. The stop at $117 protects against a macro deterioration that overwhelms the PLTR-specific thesis before earnings.
bull_case: Q2 2026 earnings Aug 3 AH: US government revenue +40%+ YoY driven by AIP DoD deployments under the Maven Smart System and drone-defense classifications; US commercial revenue annualized run rate $620M+ (above $600M threshold); Q3 FY26 guidance raises full-year revenue above Street consensus. Iran escalation produces a DoD supplemental budget announcement in the Aug–Sep window that explicitly cites AI decision-intelligence procurement. PLTR moves 15%+ on the print toward $145–150, and institutional buyers who missed the pre-earnings entry accumulate on the Aug 4 open — PLTR reaches $155 within two weeks of earnings.
bear_case: Q2 2026 earnings disappoint on the government revenue line: Maven deployments are delayed by procurement cycle timing (contracts awarded but not recognized), and US commercial growth decelerates to <30% YoY as AIP bootcamp conversion rates plateau. The Iran DoD catalyst does not appear in Q2 revenue (deployments are lagged by quarters from contracts). Options pricing correctly anticipates a large move, but the direction is down 12–15% toward $110–112. GDP hot print before earnings (8:30 AM July 30) provides the macro headwind that pre-positions growth equities lower ahead of the Aug 3 catalyst, potentially pulling PLTR to $117 before earnings resolve.
invalidation: GDP >2.5% annualized at 8:30 AM July 30 AND AAPL AH miss tonight (macro headwind + quality-rotation leader fails simultaneously): exit immediately, do not wait for Aug 3 catalyst. A daily close below $117 before earnings exits the position regardless of Iran news. Post-earnings: if Q2 government revenue growth below 20% YoY with no positive Q3 guidance raise — the DoD escalation thesis has not yet reached the revenue line; exit the remaining position at the Aug 4 open.
